title_en: Daqing Zhu'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhu'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch v. China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 224 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 29 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China provide clear provisions on the hierarchical jurisdiction and territorial jurisdiction for the enforcement of arbitration cases, which are mandatory and binding. With respect to the enforcement of an arbitration award, there are only two connecting points for determining jurisdiction: the domicile of the person subject to enforcement and the location of the property subject to enforcement. The Civil Procedure Law is a law of a public law nature, and what is not expressly authorized by law is prohibited. Although the Civil Procedure Law does not explicitly prohibit the parties from negotiating to choose the court of enforcement jurisdiction, the parties' choice of jurisdiction for enforcement cases is limited to the above two connecting points. The parties may only choose, in accordance with the law, to file an application for enforcement with one of the courts that has jurisdiction. The provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on appearance jurisdiction are applicable to litigation proceedings, not to enforcement proceedings. Therefore, if the parties choose, by agreement, or otherwise determine by default (such as by not raising a jurisdictional objection or waiving a jurisdictional objection) to apply to a court without jurisdiction for enforcement, such a choice shall not be supported.

full_text_en:
Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch v. China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction contract

【Ruling Summary】

Article 224 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China provide clear provisions on the hierarchical jurisdiction and territorial jurisdiction for the enforcement of arbitration cases, which are compulsory and binding. Regarding the enforcement of an arbitration award, there are only two connecting points for determining jurisdiction: one is the domicile of the person against whom enforcement is sought, and the other is the location of the property to be enforced. The Civil Procedure Law is a legal norm of a public law nature; what the law does not grant is prohibited. Although the Civil Procedure Law does not expressly prohibit the parties from negotiating to choose the court for enforcement jurisdiction, it limits the parties' choice of jurisdiction for enforcement cases to the two aforementioned connecting points. The parties may only lawfully choose to file an enforcement application with one of the courts that has jurisdiction. The provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on jurisdiction by appearance are applicable to litigation proceedings and not to enforcement proceedings. Therefore, where the parties select, by agreement or by default actions such as failing to raise or waiving an objection to jurisdiction, to apply for enforcement to a court that does not have jurisdiction, such actions shall not be upheld.

Enforcement Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Zhi Shen Zi No. 42

Complainant: Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 6, Lane 52, Wolitun Street, Longfeng District, Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Huo Ruijin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Dong Peng, lawyer from Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lu Luwei, lawyer from Beijing Yixing Law Firm.

Complainant (person against whom enforcement is sought): Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch. Domicile: No. 11, Dongmen Street, Qufu City, Jining City, Shandong Province.

Responsible Person: Hao Dekun, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Dong Peng, lawyer from Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lu Luwei, lawyer from Beijing Yixing Law Firm.

Respondent (person applying for enforcement): China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 1, Kuangjian East Road, Zoucheng City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Tang Jingdong, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Guo Xianwei, Legal Counsel of the Company.

The complainants, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2014) Lu Zhi Fu Yi Zi No. 4 of the Shandong High People's Court, filed a complaint with this Court. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law for review. On June 24, 2015, this Court held a hearing, which was attended by the agents ad litem of Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, and the agent ad litem of China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. The review of this case is now concluded.

Upon review, this Court finds the following facts: In the case of China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch concerning a dispute over a construction contract, on August 5, 2011, the Qingdao Arbitration Commission rendered the Award (2008) Qing Zhong Zi No. 453, ordering Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch to pay China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. project payment of RMB 5,367,813.65, interest of RMB 840,295.79, and maintenance fees and penalties of RMB 467,000. Because the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, failed to perform the obligations determined by the effective legal instrument, the applicant for enforcement, China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd., applied for compulsory enforcement to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court on May 11, 2012. The court opened case (2012) Qing Zhi Zi No. 160 for enforcement, prepared an enforcement notice on May 16 of the same year, and sent the enforcement notice to the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, on July 20 of the same year, requiring it to perform its obligations. On the 28th of that month, the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, raised an objection to the enforcement jurisdiction of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court opened case (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 25 for review. On August 15 of the same year, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, decided to withdraw its written objection to jurisdiction because the other party agreed to resolve the matter through negotiation. Thereafter, the parties failed to reach a consensus through negotiation, and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, continued to insist on its objection to enforcement jurisdiction. On May 19, 2013, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. raised an objection to jurisdiction with the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court. On November 12 of the same year, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 25, dismissing the objection to enforcement jurisdiction raised by Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch in this case. Subsequently, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, dissatisfied with this ruling, applied for reconsideration to the Shandong High People's Court on November 19 and 20, 2013, respectively, requesting the cancellation of this ruling.

It is also found that the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, was registered by Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. with the Qufu City Administration for Industry and Commerce on September 30, 2002, and is a branch lacking legal person status. Its business scope includes construction contracting and professional contracting. Its registered capital is RMB 0. The branch's annual inspection by the industry and commerce authorities was conducted up to 2009, and the branch is currently in a state of having its business license revoked.

It is also found that on October 5, 2012, the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, applied to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court for non-enforcement of the arbitration award. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 13 on April 19, 2013, dismissing the application of Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch for non-enforcement of the arbitration award.

It is also found that on October 8, 2012, the applicant for enforcement, China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd., applied to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court to add Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. as a person against whom enforcement is sought. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 24 on November 13, 2013, adding Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. as a person against whom enforcement is sought in case (2012) Qing Zhi Zi No. 160. Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with this ruling, raised an objection to enforcement to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2014) Qing Zhi Yi Zi No. 10 on May 6, 2014, dismissing the enforcement objection of Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd.

It is also found that on November 12, 2012, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2012) Qing Zhi Zi No. 160, ruling to conclude the current enforcement procedure.

The Shandong High People's Court held that, pursuant to Article 3, Paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in Enforcement Proceedings, the person against whom enforcement is sought in this case, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, raised an objection to enforcement jurisdiction within the statutory period. During the review by the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, decided to withdraw its objection to jurisdiction and agreed that the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court could exercise jurisdiction over this case. This was its true intention, and there was no evidence that it violated the principle of voluntariness; therefore, it did not violate the law. On October 25, 2012, the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, applied to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court for non-enforcement of the arbitration award, indicating its recognition that the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court had enforcement jurisdiction over this case. It was not improper for the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court to lawfully dismiss the objections of Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch. In summary, the grounds for reconsideration of the applicants for reconsideration, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, were not established. The court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2014) Lu Zhi Fu Yi Zi No. 4 on January 27, 2014, dismissing the reconsideration applications of Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch.

The complainants, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. and Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, dissatisfied with the above ruling, filed a complaint with this Court, requesting the cancellation of the Enforcement Ruling (2014) Lu Zhi Fu Yi Zi No. 4 of the Shandong High People's Court and the designation of a court with jurisdiction for enforcement. The main reasons are as follows: First, according to Article 224 and Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the relevant provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, an arbitration award may be enforced by the intermediate people's court at the domicile of the person against whom enforcement is sought or at the location of the property to be enforced. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court is neither the court at the domicile of the person against whom enforcement is sought nor the court at the location of the property to be enforced; therefore, it has no authority to docket, accept, or exercise jurisdiction over this case. Second, Chinese laws and judicial interpretations do not provide for the parties' right to freely choose a court outside the statutory jurisdiction for enforcement. Even if both parties choose a court outside the statutory jurisdiction for enforcement, this violates the mandatory provisions of the law and should be deemed an invalid agreement. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court and the Shandong High People's Court were wrong to hold that the exercise of jurisdiction over this case was the true intention of the parties and did not violate the law.

China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd. argued in its defense that, because the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, claimed that it had special relationships with the Jining Intermediate People's Court and the Daqing Intermediate People's Court, and if enforcement was carried out by those courts, the creditor's rights could not be realized. Furthermore, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch's application to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court for revocation of the arbitration award was dismissed. Therefore, it applied for enforcement to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court. After the case was docketed for enforcement, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, filed objections to jurisdiction and applications for non-enforcement of the arbitration award to delay and evade enforcement, resulting in the arbitration award not being enforced to this day.

Upon review, this Court holds that the focus of this case is whether the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court has jurisdiction over the enforcement of this case. Article 224 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China provide clear provisions on the hierarchical jurisdiction and territorial jurisdiction for the enforcement of arbitration cases, which are compulsory and binding. For the enforcement of an arbitration award, there are only two connecting points for determining jurisdiction: one is the domicile of the person against whom enforcement is sought; the other is the location of the property to be enforced. The Civil Procedure Law is a legal norm of a public law nature; what the law does not grant is prohibited. Although the Civil Procedure Law does not expressly prohibit the parties from negotiating to choose the enforcement jurisdiction court, the law limits the parties' choice of jurisdiction for enforcement cases to the two aforementioned connecting points. The parties may only lawfully choose to file an enforcement application with one of the courts that has jurisdiction among these two connecting points, and may not change the enforcement jurisdiction court provided by law in any way. The provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China on jurisdiction by appearance are applicable to litigation proceedings; there is no legal basis or doctrinal basis for their application in enforcement proceedings. Therefore, where the parties select, by agreement or by default actions such as failing to raise or waiving an objection to jurisdiction, to vest jurisdiction in a court that does not have enforcement jurisdiction, this does not comply with the provisions of the law. In the present case, neither the domicile nor the location of the property of the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, falls within the jurisdiction of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court. Therefore, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court does not have jurisdiction over the enforcement of this case. The applicant for enforcement, China Coal No. 68 Engineering Co., Ltd., on the ground that the person against whom enforcement is sought claimed to have special relationships with the courts at the domicile or property location, did not apply for enforcement to a court with jurisdiction but instead applied for enforcement to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, which lacks jurisdiction. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, knowing it had no jurisdiction, accepted the case, which does not comply with the law. The person against whom enforcement is sought in this case, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, raised an objection to enforcement jurisdiction within the statutory period. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court should have reviewed it lawfully and determined whether the objection was well-founded according to the law. Although during this period, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, decided to withdraw its objection to jurisdiction and also applied to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court for non-enforcement of the arbitration award, the above actions of the parties cannot change the provisions of the law and vest the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court with jurisdiction over the enforcement of this case. In summary, the grounds of complaint of Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch are valid. The handling of the enforcement jurisdiction objection in this case by the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court and the Shandong High People's Court lacked legal basis and should be corrected. At the time the enforcement jurisdiction was determined, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. was not a party to this case; it was a party added by the court upon application of another party. It had no right to raise objections to the determination of jurisdiction in this case. Given that Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd. is not a party to the arbitration award case, the determination of the enforcement jurisdiction court for the arbitration award case cannot be based on its domicile or property location. It should be based on the domicile of the person against whom enforcement is sought or the location of the property to be enforced in the arbitration award case, i.e., the intermediate people's court at the domicile of the person against whom enforcement is sought, Daqing Zhuan'an Construction Engineering Group Co., Ltd., Qufu Branch, or at the location of the property to be enforced has jurisdiction. Given that the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court does not have jurisdiction over the enforcement of this case, to facilitate the smooth enforcement of this case by the court with enforcement jurisdiction and to eliminate obstacles in the enforcement procedure, the relevant enforcement rulings made by the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court that do not involve property control measures should be revoked together. In conclusion, pursuant to Article 224 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 129 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Work of the People's Courts in Enforcement (for Trial Implementation), and by reference to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

1. The Enforcement Ruling (2014) Lu Zhi Fu Yi Zi No. 4 of the Shandong High People's Court is revoked.

2. The Enforcement Rulings (2012) Qing Zhi Zi No. 160, (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 25, (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 13, (2013) Qing Zhi Cai Zi No. 24, and (2014) Qing Zhi Yi Zi No. 10 made by the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court are revoked.

3. The applicant for enforcement shall apply for enforcement to the people's court with jurisdiction in accordance with the law.

This ruling shall become legally effective upon service.

Presiding Judge: He Dongning
Acting Judge: Xue Guizhong
Acting Judge: Xiang Guohui

September 16, 2015

Clerk: Zhang Qiaoyun
